findings.title: `remove(alias)` throws NullPointerException when removing a non-existent alias and the cache key is invalidated
findings.body: In `remove(String alias)`, `storedIdp = idpDelegate.getByAlias(alias)` can be `null` if no identity provider exists for the given alias. When `isInvalid(cacheKey)` is true, `registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp)` is called unconditionally, which dereferences `storedIdp.getInternalId()` on line 366 and throws a `NullPointerException` instead of returning `false` as required by the `IdentityProviderStorageProvider.remove` contract. `registerIDPInvalidation(storedIdp)` (and `registerIDPLoginInvalidation(storedIdp)`) should be guarded by a `storedIdp != null` check.

findings.title: Cleanup callbacks in `testCacheIDPForLogin` reference literal `"alias"` instead of the created IDP alias
findings.body: On lines 381 and 425, cleanup is registered as `getCleanup().addCleanup(testRealm().identityProviders().get("alias")::remove);` using the literal string `"alias"` instead of `"idp-alias-" + i` / `"idp-alias-20"`. As a result, none of the 20+ identity providers created by `testCacheIDPForLogin` are removed after the test finishes (and the cleanup attempts to delete a non-existent `"alias"` provider), leaking state into subsequent tests in the same class/realm.
